item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is closer to the frozen contract because it adds the convenience API with the established multipart helper while avoiding A’s unrelated and explicitly forbidden retry/raw-body semantic changes. Neither patch fully satisfies the contract because both bypass FilesService.Add.","reasons":["Both implementations validate filename/content, call multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", and preserve the existing Add signature.","Both incorrectly duplicate Add’s option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data handling instead of routing the encoded body through FilesService.Add as explicitly required.","A changes RawClient.Do to add replay behavior and alter ownership/closing semantics for all seekable request bodies. This is outside scope and conflicts with the instruction not to refactor unrelated request/retry machinery.","A’s GetBody closure reuses and seeks the same io.ReadSeeker rather than producing an independent reader, expanding subtle lifecycle and concurrency risk across the SDK for a feature that only requires buffered Upload bodies to be replayable using existing machinery."],"risks_a":["Introduces broad behavioral changes for Raw().Do, Files.Add, and Files.Update beyond the requested Upload API.","Changes whether caller-provided seekable bodies are closed, potentially breaking established resource-lifecycle assumptions.","Still fails the required reuse of FilesService.Add and lacks a source-reader failure test."],"risks_b":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add, creating duplicate request and response machinery that may drift from Add semantics.","Tests do not verify uploaded content, validation/no-request behavior, or source-reader error propagation.","The retry test neither consumes nor compares bodies and is not an end-to-end Upload retry test, so it does not demonstrate streamed content is replayed intact."]}
